name: Derrick Rose
description: Derrick Rose (born October 4, 1988, in Chicago) is the hometown point guard whose rise from Simeon Career Academy to the Chicago Bulls made him the most beloved Chicago athlete of his generation. At Simeon, wearing No. 25 in honor of Ben Wilson, he led the Wolverines to back-to-back Illinois state championships in 2006 and 2007 — the first Chicago public school to repeat — then took Memphis to the 2008 NCAA title game. Drafted first overall by his hometown Bulls in 2008, he won Rookie of the Year in 2009 and, in 2011, became the youngest Most Valuable Player in NBA history at twenty-two, leading Chicago to a league-best 62–20 record. A torn ACL in the 2012 playoffs and further knee injuries reshaped his career; he played on for four more franchises before retiring in 2024. The Bulls announced they will retire his No. 1, making him the fifth player so honored by the franchise.

name: Damn Right, I've Got the Blues
Do the Right Thing
description: Do the Right Thing, written, produced, and directed by Spike Lee and released by Universal Pictures on June 30, 1989, after a Cannes premiere that May 19, unfolds over the hottest day of the summer on one Bedford-Stuyvesant block, where the wall of photographs in Sal's pizzeria — famous Italian-Americans only — becomes the argument the neighborhood has been postponing. In 1999, in its first year of eligibility, the Library of Congress selected it for the National Film Registry — among the very few films honored that early, an institutional verdict delivered a decade out. The Academy gave it two nominations, for Lee's original screenplay and for Danny Aiello's supporting performance; its absence from the Best Picture slate was protested from the ceremony's own stage and remains a reference-point snub in awards history. In Sight and Sound's 2022 critics' poll of the greatest films ever made, it ranked twenty-fourth. For this graph, Do the Right Thing is the film shelf's hinge: the work that announced the modern Black American cinema to the world and has never left the argument since.

name: Doc Rivers
description: Glenn Anton “Doc” Rivers (born October 13, 1961, in Chicago) is the Chicago-born guard who became one of the most successful head coaches in NBA history. Raised in Maywood, he starred at Proviso East High School and Marquette University, which retired his No. 31, and was USA Basketball's Male Athlete of the Year in 1982. Drafted 31st overall by Atlanta in 1983, he played thirteen NBA seasons for the Hawks, Clippers, Knicks, and Spurs and was an All-Star in 1988. As a head coach he won the 2000 NBA Coach of the Year award with Orlando and the 2008 NBA championship with Boston, then coached the Los Angeles Clippers, Philadelphia 76ers, and Milwaukee Bucks, reaching 1,194 regular-season wins — sixth in league history. Named one of the fifteen greatest coaches in NBA history, he was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2026 and joined NBC Sports as a game analyst for the 2026–27 season.

Raised on church piano, he co-wrote Black Men United’s “U Will Know” (1994) before Brown Sugar (1995) joined classic R&B craft to hip-hop rhythm and stayed on the Billboard 200 for 65 weeks. name: Dr. Dre
description: Dr. Dre, born Andre Romelle Young on February 18, 1965, in Compton, California, is an American rapper, producer, and entrepreneur whose work shaped West Coast hip-hop across three distinct chapters. First, as a founding member of N.W.A, whose Straight Outta Compton (1988) broke gangsta rap nationally, Dre's layered production carried the group's records, and N.W.A was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016. Second, as a solo artist: after co-founding Death Row Records, his debut The Chronic (1992) popularized G-funk and won a Grammy for 'Let Me Ride,' and 2001 (1999) and Compton (2015) completed a spare, three-album solo catalog. Third, as a producer-executive: he founded Aftermath Entertainment in 1996 and signed or developed Snoop Dogg, Eminem, 50 Cent, and Kendrick Lamar, whom he signed in 2012. With Jimmy Iovine he co-founded Beats Electronics, which Apple acquired in 2014 in a deal reported at about three billion dollars, and he has remained a central, if selective, production presence since.

name: Duke Ellington
description: Duke Ellington was an orchestra leader associated with the Swing Era. He performed frequently at Chicago's Regal Theater, the Bronzeville movie-and-stage palace at 4719 South Parkway, where he appeared among the theater's documented notable performers of the 1920s–40s alongside Nat “King” Cole, Cab Calloway, Louis Armstrong, and Ella Fitzgerald. The Duke Ellington Band also played Chicago's Tivoli Theatre on January 28 and 30, 1960, dates preserved in Chicago Defender citations. Ellington's recording reach extended to Chicago's Universal Recording, whose sessions included him among their artists, and gospel singer Mahalia Jackson recorded “Come Sunday” with him, a collaboration documented as bridging gospel and jazz.

name: DJ Khaled
description: DJ Khaled, born Khaled Mohamed Khaled on November 26, 1975, in New Orleans, Louisiana, to Palestinian immigrant parents, is an American DJ, record producer, executive, and media personality who built a career as hip-hop's great convener. Raised around his parents' Arabic music and early rap and soul, he worked in New Orleans record stores, met Birdman and Lil Wayne in the early 1990s, and moved through Miami pirate and commercial radio, notably WEDR 99 Jamz, and a DJ role with Terror Squad, before releasing his debut Listennn... the Album in 2006. He founded We the Best Music Group and served as president of Def Jam South from 2009. His albums became star-stacked events: Major Key (2016) was his first Billboard 200 number one, Grateful (2017) repeated the feat behind the Hot 100 number one 'I'm the One,' and Father of Asahd (2019) brought his first Grammy win. Khaled Khaled (2021) and God Did (2022) gave him four Billboard 200 number ones in total, while his motivational social-media presence and book The Keys extended his reach well beyond records.

name: Dyon Brooks
description: Mojo Brookzz — born Dyon Brooks — is a Chicago-born stand-up comedian, actor, writer and producer who built a national audience online before he built one on stage. Raised in Chicago, he began posting comic sketches to Facebook and Instagram, and series such as 'Thawt in My House,' his mother and grandmother impersonations and the character 'Mr. James' carried him to more than 5.5 million followers across platforms. Nick Cannon hand-picked him for season 21 of Wild 'N Out, and he became a featured comic on the We Them Ones arena tour with Mike Epps. His 2024 Unhand Me Now tour sold out every show, and the follow-up I Know You F*ckin' Lying tour sold out some forty cities, including the Chicago Theatre and two nights at Chicago's Wintrust Arena. In 2025 he was named one of Variety's 10 Comics to Watch and took the male lead in Tyler Perry's Netflix series Miss Governor, which spent multiple weeks in the platform's Top 10. His writing for Chicago Bears campaigns contributed to a Midwest Emmy win, and his debut stand-up special premiered in October 2026.
